summary: Washington County, Maine tower in Baring, about 100 feet, built around 1937 inside Moosehorn refuge; register says removed circa 1954; no site description found.

facts.status_note: Removed circa 1954 according to the register; no source describes what remains on the summit

access.note: Inside Moosehorn National Wildlife Refuge, which visitors can enjoy by car, on foot, by bike or on horseback; no source describes a route to the summit

events.note: Built around 1937 per the Sun Journal (approximate); about 100 feet tall
Photo taken from the tower in 1951, credited to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
Registered September 15, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

evidence.supports: on Bald Mountain in Baring, inside the Moosehorn refuge

notes_for_editor: Not cited because not read: a Facebook group post and a YouTube video description (seen only in search results) say a Civilian Conservation Corps camp (Co. 1129) built the tower in 1937-39 and that it lasted into the 1960s. That conflicts with the register's circa 1954 removal. Worth checking before publication. The Living New Deal page returned HTTP 403, so it was not read. Do not confuse with 'Washington Bald Mountain' (Maine Atlas caption: a 55-foot tower built 1918), a different site at 45.09818, -67.92316. The Forest Lookouts page for this site has only a location line and adds nothing. The 'tallest in Maine' claim is the Sun Journal's; not independently checked. Brief record consistent: gone, FFLOS US 85, registered 2008, Baring. Brief has no height; 30.5 m comes from the article's 100 feet.
